scope: Review only the applicability of current journal copyright and website-license notices to the digitized 1990 article. This is not a new review or transcription of its fish-catch data.

itemIdentity.title: Survey of Migratory Fishes in Pansipit River and Taal Lake

rightsSources.finding: The current TPJF copyright policy says authors submitting manuscripts agree to CC BY-NC 4.0 and retain copyright. The policy page does not provide an effective date establishing that the terms apply to the 1990 article.

The current Author Guidelines page carries a site-content footer stating CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise stated. It does not explicitly identify the legacy volume 21 PDF or explain its relationship to the policy page's CC BY-NC 4.0 terms.
The official article HTML page still displays an abstract about Tayabas Bay fishing gears rather than the titled Pansipit/Taal article. It does not resolve the license for the legacy item.

pdfLicenseCheck.method: Rechecked the official scanned PDF's searchable text and the full-text rendering for copyright, Creative Commons, rights, and license statements.
pdfLicenseCheck.finding: No item-level license or copyright notice was found in the PDF text. Absence from its searchable text does not establish that the item is unprotected or that no separate rights condition applies.

decision.rationale: The modern journal policy, the current site-wide footer, and the legacy 1990 PDF do not unambiguously establish which license applies to this archived article. Do not select either CC BY-NC 4.0 or CC BY 4.0 by assumption. Preserve the existing research-only status.

nextActions: Continue with independently reusable, location-resolved historical specimen records and current surveys; do not wait on this rights question to advance other waterbodies.
If table reuse becomes necessary, seek explicit item-level confirmation from the rights holder or use a separately licensed dataset that independently reports the same facts.
nonClaims: The journal's current licensing language is not treated as retroactive permission for the 1990 article.
No current presence, whole-waterbody census, abundance, diet, safety, catchability, geometry, or legal rule is inferred.
